entries.claim: The draft check is vulnerable to a time-of-check/time-of-use race, so it does not guarantee that the release is still a draft when the later upload and edit occur.
entries.failure_scenario: The lookup returns exactly `true`, then another actor or workflow publishes the release while this script downloads, verifies, and signs artifacts. The script subsequently continues to `release upload --clobber` and `release edit` against that now-published release, replacing its signature assets and marking it latest. Lookup failures and unexpected outputs fail closed, but this concurrent transition leaves the original finding open.

counter_evidence.note: Only an account with write access can publish a draft. The release workflow makes the draft once and never publishes it, and release-check.yml runs on release: published with contents: read only (PLAN-2 must-be-true; the workflow test pins it). So the only actor who can publish during the signing window is the owner himself, from a second terminal, while he is typing his passphrase into this one. GitHub offers no upload-only-if-draft call, so no script can close the window completely. The finding the fix was asked to close, running against an already-published tag, is closed at scripts/sign-release.sh:62-65 and fails closed on a lookup error. Low.
